official.deadline_note: The application window is annual: it opens 1 June and the deadline is 31 July each year (FAQ), so the next deadline after the closed 2027-intake round falls on 31 July 2027. The 2027-intake round closed on 31 July 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2027 intake round: application period 1 June to 31 July 2026, studies start September/October 2027; next (2028 intake) round expected to open 1 June 2027
official.status_note: The application period for the 2027 intake for all seven higher education institutions ran from 1 June until 31 July 2026 and is closed; the selection committee meets in October/November 2026 and all applicants are to be informed in writing after the selection process, expected December 2026/January 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: "DAAD scholarship holders are exempt from paying tuition fees." The FAQ adds that a registration fee must still be paid for each semester.
benefits: Scholarships of currently EUR 992 per month for master's courses at German higher education institutions
Health insurance cover in Germany; health, accident and liability insurance in Germany are covered by the scholarship
Fixed travel allowances (lump sums) for travel between Germany and the respective developing or emerging country
A study and research grant of EUR 460 each year
Rent subsidies and family supplements (partner/children allowances), as applicable
A preceding German language course in Germany lasting up to four months; participation is mandatory
Accompanying support from programme coordinators, special tutoring in small groups, networking events and tailor-made workshops
eligibility: Graduates from developing and emerging countries with a first university degree (bachelor or equivalent)
Well-qualified first university degree with above-average grades (upper third) in Social and Political Sciences, Law, Economics, Public Policy and Administration, or a related field
Willing to actively contribute to the social, political and economic development of the home country or region
Practical experience relevant to the programme (professional experience, internships, political or social commitment); specific requirements vary by master's course
Both young graduates without professional experience and mid-career professionals may apply
The last university degree should not date back more than six years at the time of application (date of issue not before 1 January 2020)
Candidates who have spent more than the past 15 months in a country not listed on the DAC list are not eligible
Candidates who already hold a master's degree must make a well-argued case for funding of another postgraduate degree
The first degree must be completed by the closing date of the application round (31 July)
requirements: All applications must be submitted in English or German
Apply for up to two of the seven listed master's courses, with a clear prioritisation in the letter of motivation
Submit the DAAD application form and required documents directly to the master's course(s), not to the DAAD
Complete the DAAD "Application Form" only once, indicating the selected course(s)
Only applications including all required documents will be considered; incomplete or formally incorrect applications may be rejected
Each master's course has its own additional selection criteria (degree, grades, language skills, practical experience) that must be met in addition to the DAAD's
documents: Ticked-off checklist and list of criteria, signed by hand (print, sign, scan), with place and date of issue
DAAD application form (completed once, stating chosen course[s])

A single letter of motivation, max. two pages, with date of issue, explaining academic, professional and personal reasons and the choice and ranking of course(s) (same letter to both courses if applying for two)
Curriculum vitae in reverse chronological order in Europass format including date of issue; gaps of three months or more must be explained
Copies of higher education degree certificates, with certified translation if not in German or English; the date of issue should not be before 1 January 2020
Copy of the full transcript of records including an explanation of the grading system, with certified translation if not in German or English

Confirmations of relevant professional experience or internships and/or proof of political activities or community service on headed paper with original (not scanned) or code-certified digital signature, date of issue and stamp

A current written reference from the current employer, or from a university lecturer only if currently a student, on headed paper with original or code-certified digital signature, date of issue and stamp
Applicants from India and from the People's Republic of China must submit an APS Certificate
selection_criteria: A conclusive account of academic, professional and personal motivation for studying in Germany and for choosing and prioritising the master's courses
Motivation that clearly relates to the goals of the Helmut-Schmidt-Programme
Practical experience relevant to the programme (professional experience, internships, political activities or service to the community, such as volunteering or work for charities or NGOs)
A first higher education degree completed with above-average grades (upper third)
coverage: Exemption from tuition fees at the host institution
Health, accident and liability insurance in Germany
Fixed travel allowances (lump sums) for travel between Germany and the home developing/emerging country
Study and research grant of EUR 460 each year
Rent subsidy and/or allowances for spouse and/or children, as applicable
Mandatory German language course in Germany of up to four months before the master's studies

Deviation for the Social Protection course (blended learning): a sur place rate of EUR 500 per month is paid in the 4th semester (mandatory online semester in the country of origin or another developing/emerging country) instead of the usual scholarship rate
application_method: Read the DAAD selection criteria in the checklist and address every point
Complete the DAAD application form once and indicate the selected master's course(s) (maximum two)
Rank the two chosen courses in order of preference in a single letter of motivation and send the same letter to both courses
Send the application package directly to the master's course(s) of choice (Erfurt: apply online); do not send it to the DAAD
If nominated by email by the DAAD after the university shortlist, upload full documents to the DAAD portal
official.application_route: Apply directly to your chosen master's course(s) at up to two of the seven participating universities using each university's own procedure, enclosing the single DAAD application form and document set - applications to the DAAD itself are not forwarded.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to candidates from developing and emerging countries (see the DAAD list of countries). Applicants who have resided in a country not on the DAC list for more than the past 15 months at the time of the application deadline are not eligible; those living in Germany for less than 15 months at the deadline may apply.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is specifically designed for graduates of developing and emerging countries on the DAAD/DAC list of eligible countries.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: First degree in Social and Political Sciences, Law, Economics, Public Policy and Administration or a related field relevant to social, political and economic development; the scholarship is available only for the seven listed master's courses. The programme is funded by the German Federal Foreign Office.
official.duration: Master's courses of two to four semesters depending on the course (Development and Governance: 2 semesters; the other listed courses: 4 semesters), preceded by a mandatory German language course in Germany of up to four months; courses start in September/October 2027.
official.description: With the Helmut-Schmidt-Programme the DAAD strives to contribute to promoting good governance and civil society structures in developing and emerging countries. It offers future leaders master's courses in disciplines of special relevance for social, political and economic development and prepares them in a practice-oriented course for responsible positions in or for their home regions. The programme is funded by the Federal Foreign Office.
official.region: Germany; applicants from developing and emerging countries (DAAD list of countries) worldwide
official.program_type: DAAD master's scholarship (funded by the Federal Foreign Office) for Public Policy and Good Governance at selected German universities
official.english_requirement: The selected master's courses have an international orientation and are taught in English, and proof of English language skills is a required application document. The required level and accepted certificates vary by master's course and are set by each course, so the DAAD does not publish a single score; applicants whose previous studies were taught in English must check the individual course websites whether a certificate is needed.

verification.notes: All amounts, deadlines, coverage and documents were taken from the DAAD's own current announcement (05/2026) and FAQ (05/2026) PDFs linked from the official programme and scholarship-database pages on daad.de; the 2027-intake round (1 June - 31 July 2026) is closed as of the verification date.

applicant_utility.summary: This DAAD award pays EUR 992 per month, waives tuition, covers German health, accident and liability insurance, adds a EUR 460 annual study and research grant and lump-sum travel money, and starts with a mandatory German language course of up to four months in Germany. The catch is route: you never apply to the DAAD itself - you apply to a maximum of two of the seven listed master's courses, and the university shortlist is what puts you in front of the selection committee in October/November. Watch two dated rules that quietly end applications: your last degree must have been issued on or after 1 January 2020, and you must already hold it by 31 July. The 2027-intake window closed on 31 July 2026, so the actionable target for this cycle is the annual 1 June - 31 July window that opens in 2027 for a September/October start.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career professionals and young graduates from DAAD-list developing and emerging countries who hold an upper-third degree in law, economics, political science or public administration and want a public policy or governance master's in Germany.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country is on the DAAD list of countries and that you have not spent more than the last 15 months outside DAC-list countries
Check the admission and language requirements of your chosen course directly with the course office (contact emails are listed in the announcement) before 1 June
Print and hand-sign the DAAD checklist, then scan it with place and date of issue filled in
Build a Europass CV in reverse chronological order and explain every gap of three months or more
Request employer/university references early on headed paper with an original or code-certified digital signature, stamp and date of issue - scanned-typed signatures are rejected
Arrange certified translations of degree certificates and transcripts, plus the grading-system explanation, if they are not in German or English
Secure English proof that your chosen course accepts; check whether the course waives the certificate for English-taught degrees
Applicants from India and China: start the APS certificate process months ahead, since it must accompany the application
common_rejection_risks: Sending the application to the DAAD instead of the master's course - such applications are not forwarded and are not returned
Addressing more than two institutions or omitting a clear, consistent ranking of first and second choice in the motivation letter
A last degree issued before 1 January 2020, or graduation that only completes after 31 July
Below-average grades - an upper-third result is an essential criterion
Missing hand signature or stamp on the checklist, experience confirmations or the reference
Unexplained CV gaps of three months or more
Applying for a course where you do not meet that course's own entry, language or practical-experience requirements
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: A semester registration fee must be paid at the host university and is not covered; anything before the first scholarship payment (visa, travel beyond the lump sum, initial deposits) is on you. The DAAD does not publish the registration fee or travel lump-sum amounts, so budget from the host university's own fee page.
document_audit: The checklist must be signed by hand (wet ink) - a typed or pasted signature is a formal defect
The Europass template carries no date; you must add the date of issue yourself
One single motivation letter, max two pages, used for both courses if applying for two, with the ranking justified inside it
Experience and service confirmations need headed paper, an original or code-certified digital signature, a stamp and the date of issue, with certified translations where needed
Degree certificates and full transcripts must be legible, translated and accompanied by the grading system explanation
alerts: The 2027-intake round closed on 31 July 2026; the next round opens 1 June with a 31 July deadline, and selection sits in October/November with decisions expected December/January - plan a roughly 14-month runway to enrolment
The German language course of up to four months in Germany is mandatory, not optional, and pushes the start of the master's itself into September/October
On the Social Protection course at Bonn-Rhein-Sieg the 4th-semester online semester is paid at a sur place rate of EUR 500 per month instead of EUR 992
Already holding a master's degree requires a well-argued case for funding a second postgraduate degree
Only upload documents to the DAAD portal if the DAAD emails you a nomination after the university shortlist; unsolicited uploads are not part of the process
The participating-course list has changed between years (now seven), so re-check it each cycle before applying
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You submit the DAAD form plus the document set to your chosen course(s) through the university's own procedure by 31 July; the course shortlists and nominates, the DAAD emails nominees to upload full documents to the DAAD portal, and the joint committee decides with written decisions to all applicants around December/January.
